transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. It's really nice to meet you too. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, I'm here because... well, I've been having just a little bit of a... a silly issue at work. I hope it's okay that I'm bringing this up. I'm a jeweler, and lately, when customers ask me a really simple question—like, just asking when a ring repair will be ready—my answer just gets a little, um, jumbled, I guess? 

Like, I'll start out fine, but then my explanation kind of drifts from the shop invoices to... I don't know, garden soil, and then suddenly I'm talking about my mortgage papers. I can see them just completely losing the thread, and I feel so terrible making people confused. I really just want to be helpful and give them a good experience, you know? 

Am I explaining that right? I hope that makes sense.
When your speech gets jumbled, do your thoughts also feel like they jump from one topic to another without you meaning them to?

Oh, um, yes... I suppose that's a really good way to put it. Like I was just saying about the... the ring repairs and the garden soil, it's like my brain just sort of skips ahead without my permission? 

I really don't mean to do it. It's just a little bit of a scatterbrained moment, I think. I try so hard to stay focused on the customer, I promise, it's just... the thoughts kind of tumble together before I can catch them, and then I end up talking about my mortgage out loud. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. It's not all the time! Does that sound like a normal thing that just happens when people get a little tired or stressed, maybe?
Have you been feeling unusually high, euphoric, or excessively cheerful lately?

Oh, goodness, no. I wouldn't say I've felt high or anything like that. If anything, I've just been a little... well, maybe just a tiny bit down lately? But definitely not overly cheerful or euphoric. I try to keep a smile on for the customers, of course, because that's just polite, but I don't feel unusually happy. Is it okay that I haven't been feeling that way? I hope I'm answering your questions the right way.
Have you been hearing voices when no one is there?

Um... well, I guess... sometimes? I hope that doesn't sound too strange. It's really nothing major, I promise. Just... sometimes when the shop is completely quiet, I might hear, um, a woman kind of muttering my name? And it sounds like it's coming from the polishing room. 

And, oh, occasionally I'll smell burning metal, even when I know for a fact all the torches are turned off. It just feels so real in the moment that I always go back there to check, just to be safe. But it's probably just my imagination playing tricks on me, right? Like maybe just the ventilation system or an echo from the street? I really hope you don't think I'm crazy for mentioning it. Is it normal to have little moments like that?
Did these problems start after a head injury, seizure, or another medical illness?

Oh, no, definitely not. I haven't had any head injuries or seizures, or... or any big medical illnesses. I'm actually quite healthy, physically, I mean. I'm always very careful in the shop so I don't have any accidents. 

So, no, nothing like that at all. I hope that's a good thing? I'm sorry if I'm not giving you a very helpful medical history, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Is it okay that it didn't start from something like that?
Do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or send you special messages?

Oh... um, harm me? No, no one is trying to hurt me, I don't think. I try to be very nice to everyone who comes into the shop. 

But... well, I know it sounds a little odd, and I really hope you don't think badly of me for saying this... but sometimes I get this feeling about certain customers. It's just that they ask so many questions about the new showroom we're setting up. And I've gotten kind of convinced that they aren't really there to buy anything, but that they're coming in just to check if I'm going to miss payments on it? 

My husband always tells me they're just being friendly and making conversation, and he's usually right about these things. I know I probably shouldn't think that way about people. I try to just smile and answer their questions, but it just feels so pointed sometimes. Is it terrible that I get suspicious like that? I'm really trying not to let it show.
Have you found yourself losing interest in things you used to enjoy?

Well... I guess maybe a little? I feel terrible even admitting it, because I know I should be grateful for my work and I really don't want to sound like I'm just complaining. 

But... I used to just love hunting for old vintage clasps, you know? And I was even planning these little jewelry-making classes to host at the shop. I was so excited about it. But lately... I don't know, I just kind of sit there and mostly stare at the trays. It just feels like none of it is really worth starting right now. 

I really hope you don't think I'm just being lazy. I still try to keep everything organized, I promise! It's just hard to find that same joy I used to have. Do you think it's okay to go through little phases like that, where you just sort of lose your spark for a bit?
About how long have the voice-hearing and suspicious feelings been going on?

Well... let's see. I'd say... maybe around a year and eight months? That's when I first started noticing the voices and... well, those strange smells I mentioned before, and getting so worried about the customers checking up on us. 

I know that sounds like a really long time to let something go on without saying anything. I'm sorry I didn't get help sooner. I just kept hoping it was stress from the shop and that it would pass, and I really didn't want to make a fuss or bother anyone about it. I hope it's not too late to try and figure it out? I really am trying to be proactive now, I promise.
